pages.act: Guarantee of Temporary Residence and Labour
pages.text:
Kingdom of Marigni · Guarantee of Temporary Residence and Labour

Summary Leaf · Holder’s Copy

No. VS-18-0947 | Issued by the Ministry of the Interior, Kingdom of Marigni | Countersigned by the Secretariat of the Duchy of Valewisp

This summary has no legal force. The full terms are those of the Original in the Old Tongue.

Pursuant to the provisions of Chapter Fourteen of the Basic Law of Marigni concerning the temporary residence of foreign nationals, and to the customary practice governing labour on the demesnes of the Duchy of Valewisp, the Guarantor named below hereby provides full guarantee for the temporary residence and labour of the Guaranteed Person named below.

I. Guarantor
Lord of Maplegate Estate in the Duchy of Valewisp, Member of the House of Lords
Baron Ludwig von Alder

II. Scope and Term (Original, Articles II–III)
The Guaranteed Person may reside on Maplegate Estate, in the northern district of Valehold, Duchy of Valewisp, and perform services relating to its management. The permit runs for thirty full days from the date of arrival. If it is not renewed by expiry, the Guaranteed Person must leave the Kingdom of Marigni within seven days.

III. Obligations of the Guarantor (Original, Articles IV–VI)
The service comprises the operation of the estate and the supervision of its household staff and internal affairs. The place of residence is the main house of the estate. The Guarantor is jointly liable for the conduct of the Guaranteed Person during the permit, and provides lodging, board and remuneration of 150 guldmark.

IV. Obligations of the Guaranteed Person (Original, Article VII)
The Guaranteed Person shall obey the laws of the Kingdom of Marigni, the ordinances of the Duchy of Valewisp and the customs of the local jurisdiction; shall not act beyond the scope of this permit; and shall not publicly propagate any religious, ideological or political doctrine contrary to Chapter VII of the Basic Law. This leaf must be carried at all times and produced to officers of the Secretariat on request.

V. Protection of the Sacred Flame (Original, Article VIII)
During the permit, the Guaranteed Person enjoys the protection of the Sacred Flame on the same terms as subjects of Marigni, and bears the corresponding duties.

VI. Execution (Original, Article XV)
The Original is made in three counterparts and takes effect when signed by the Guarantor and the Guaranteed Person and countersigned by the Secretariat. The counterparts are held by the Ministry, the Secretariat and the Guarantor.

Signature of the Guarantor: von Alder    Date: 27 September 2018
Received by the Guaranteed Person: ______    Date: 28 September 2018

Ministry of the Interior, Kingdom of Marigni · Seal Forged in the Sacred Flame | Secretariat of the Duchy of Valewisp · Seal of the Duchy

pages.heading: What the Agent Said
pages.text:
“The Duchy of Valewisp. Maplegate Estate.”

When the middleman pushes the document across the desk to your side, Forgehold outside the window is wrapped in rain and fog. The silver-grey light has stained every sheet of paper in his office the same colour.

“The lord is badly in want of a temporary steward. The last one left suddenly. There was no handover at all.” He is sorting through another stack of papers. “Harvest is on them, and the estate has had nobody running it for close to three weeks.”

“Thirty-day term, board and lodging found, reasonable pay. The work over in Valewisp is not complicated, but somebody has to go at once.”

The man in front of you closes the folder.

“Though I will say this. Baron von Alder being willing to guarantee a foreigner — that is not an opportunity you see often.”

pages.heading: The Baron’s Assessment
pages.text:
Baron von Alder saw you at the Duchy House in Forgehold.

His office faces north and gets no sun. On the wall hangs a small painting of Maplegate Estate.

The meeting was short. He went through your record. He asked two questions, and the first was about your background. He did not look up while you answered.

The second question was: if there is an item of expenditure in a ledger that you cannot make sense of, what do you do first.

“That will do.” He signed the guarantee and pushed it back to the middleman. The whole thing took under fifteen minutes.

He was already reading something else as you stood up. Before you left the Duchy House you looked back once at the painting.

The Forgehold sky was still that silver grey. You had a railway ticket gripped in your hand.

pages.heading: The Kingdom’s Central Station
pages.text:
The station stands downstream on the River Forgel, at the edge of the south-bank quarter of Forgehold.

The dome of the hall is built from the grey-green stone of the northern ranges. Light pours down from narrow windows high in the dome, and the dust in the air cuts it into columns. Steel and stone meet without a gap. The buildings of this city grow out of the rock, and are then cast, block by block, by people with the patience for it.

The air on the platform is cool, carrying the metal of the rails and the damp of the river further off. A few dark grey trains stand quietly to one side. No advertising, no unnecessary markings — only the service number and the name of the destination, set in small copper letters beneath the window frames.

Your train is the 08:40. The terminus is Valehold North.

Looking back, the upper town on the north bank of the River Forgel shows only its outline in the morning fog. The spires of Crownblaze Palace, the dome of the Sanctum, and the stone span of the King’s Leap run together into one pale grey skyline. You never got over there to see it. Perhaps you never will.

You board, find your seat and stow your case.

The doors close.

pages.heading: Leaving the Mountains
pages.text:
The carriage goes dark as the train runs into the first tunnel.

Between Forgehold and Valehold the railway passes through three tunnels and two passes on the southern face of the northern ranges. These works fall directly under the Crown Lands, and every so often along the line you can see a small checkpoint and signal post beside the trackbed. The old stone walls are mossy, but the signal lamps are new.

In the tunnel the rock has drawn the warmth out of the air and left only a coolness. Coming out of the longest one, the light floods into the carriage all at once.

pages.heading: The Country Changes
pages.text:
The south face of the range and the north face are two different worlds.

The north face is the Forgehold side. Grey, bare rock, thin cover, a sky of silver as if washed. On the south face the colours suddenly multiply: conifer gives way to mixed woodland, and among the dark green firs there are gold birches and oaks in the middle of turning.

The land falls away. The valley opens out.

The train works slowly down along a tributary. Outside the window the canopy goes from grey-green to yellow-green to gold. The air is different too: less of the cold of metal, and more of a heavy sweetness, which you will learn later is leaf mould.

Now and then you pass a small town and see people on the platform waiting for other trains. They are dressed more easily than people in Forgehold, and in livelier colours.

Nobody notices you.

pages.heading: Valewisp
pages.text:
After the third halt the ground levels out altogether.

Outside the window is farmland and pasture at large. Some of the wheat spread along both banks of the river is cut already, leaving even stubble and turned black earth; some of it is still waiting, the full heads bowing in the wind, the colour of amber. On the hills further off there are stretches of woodland, and the turning of the season has dyed them into banners, each a different shade.

Cattle move slowly along the field banks. An estate shows its roof from behind a stand of trees, and thin smoke is coming off a chimney on the slate.

Whose estate is that? You do not know. The one you are going to is further north, up in the hills.

The train begins to slow.

pages.heading: Valehold North
pages.text:
Valehold’s main station is in the centre of the ducal capital, larger and more formal. The north station has only two tracks, the platform laid with grey-green slabs and weeds growing up through the joints. The waiting-room door stands half open on an empty room, and on the wall are a notice of the duchy’s forestry decrees and a timetable of this season’s markets.

You carry your luggage out off the platform. Late September afternoon; there is still some strength in the sun, but you can smell autumn in the wind.

On the open ground beside the platform stands a plain two-wheeled cart, dark wooden body, nothing about it for show. A grey-brown working horse of middling size is chewing quietly. A middle-aged man stands beside the cart in a faded dark coat, the brim of his hat low. When he sees you he gives one nod. Once you have made sure of each other, he lifts your case onto the rack at the back of the cart, then goes round to the driver’s seat and waits for you to get up.

Through all of it there is not one word of greeting.

pages.heading: The Road In
pages.text:
The cart turns onto a dirt road kept in reasonable repair, with cut wheat fields and scattered fruit trees on either side.

The wheels make a regular grinding on the hard ground, and the hooves are the only rhythm on this stretch of road. Gregor — you learn his name later — sits in front driving, his spine very straight.

Looking about, you can see dark woodland along the line of the hills to the north. To the south is open valley, and the River Valenne bends once in the distance, giving back the afternoon light. The air grows sweeter. It is very quiet, and it has been a long time since you last heard quiet like it.

At a fork the signpost gives the directions in two scripts. The upper line is in an old language you cannot read; the lower is in the common tongue. One branch points to Thornwall, the other to Millridge.

North: Maplegate Estate, four kilometres.

Gregor turns the horse.

pages.heading: The Avenue
pages.text:
At the end of the rise, maples appear suddenly along both sides of the road.

The branches meet overhead, and the two even rows make a tunnel of it. Just now, in the last days of September, the tunnel is burning: gold, copper, deep orange not yet turned red, leaf on leaf, and the light coming through the gaps and falling on the flagstones like broken gold leaf. Every so often one leaf lets go and turns slowly in the air, and comes down on the horse’s mane, and before your eyes.

The cart is under five minutes on Maplegate Avenue before the outline of buildings shows between the crowns: stone walls, roofs, a chimney smoking.

The estate.

Gregor pulls up, gets down and sets your luggage on the steps at the main door of the estate.

“Martha is inside.”

He leads the horse away towards the stable.

pages.heading: The Hall
pages.text:
The door stands open. You pick up your luggage and go in.

The hall is darker than outside and your eyes take a few seconds to adjust. Stone floor, a wooden staircase going up, and on the right a door half open, with the sound of cooking coming through it. A woman is talking, quickly, giving somebody instructions.

Then the voice stops.

“You’re here?”

She comes out from behind the door. Forties, flour on her apron, and she wipes her hands on it twice before putting one out. “Martha. The kitchen is mine.”

Martha looks you over, and does not disguise doing it.

“Road all right, was it? Gregor does not talk much. Do not take it to heart, he is like that with everybody.” She has already turned to go further in as she says it. “Supper at six. Go up and look at your room first. Elena—”

There are footsteps on the stairs.

pages.heading: The Room
pages.text:
Elena walks ahead of you with her hands folded in front of her. She does not speak, and only turns side-on at the corners to show the way.

The room at the end of the upstairs corridor. She pushes the door open and stands in the doorway.

The room is not large, and a single bed takes most of it. The sheets are fresh, the corners folded down square. A wardrobe, a desk. The desk faces the window, and the window looks onto Maplegate Avenue, which has gone dark by now.

On the dark wood of the desk there is a rectangular mark, paler than the wood around it. The four edges are very straight. Something stood there once, and stood there long enough for the wood around it to darken past it.

“Everything has been put in order.” She steps back and pulls the door to. “If you need anything else, tell me.”

Her footsteps stop for a moment in the corridor, and only then go on down the stairs.

pages.heading: The First Night
pages.text:
The estate at night is quieter than you expected.

One movement in the stable off in the distance, the wind bringing leaves down, water dripping somewhere. There is no city hum underneath. Every sound can be heard on its own, with whole silence in between them.

You open your case.

From tomorrow, this estate is yours to run for thirty days.
